body.statement: Given the exact pilot likelihood and its random information matrix \(I_m^{\mathrm{pil}}\), can one formulate and prove a valid subsequential LAN experiment indexed by an actual limit of \(I_m^{\mathrm{pil}}\), and then transfer its Gaussian decision bound to the exact finite Horvitz--Thompson action-loss contrast uniformly over arbitrary pilot-measurable actions?  Any positive answer must also prove localization, quadratic-loss uniform integrability, and the finite moving-boundary comparison; it may not replace \(I_m^{\mathrm{pil}}\) by \(I\) under the present assumptions.

obligation.what_is_open: A valid information-indexed LAN-to-exact-action theorem for arbitrary pilot-measurable actions.
obligation.obstruction: The exact pilot information matrix need not converge to the population matrix under the frozen assumptions, and no established node transfers Gaussian quadratic decision loss across exact ties and unequal inclusions.
obligation.attempted: The pilot likelihood was factored exactly and the realized information was computed.  A moment-preserving nuisance construction demonstrates that weak baseline convergence cannot supply the missing score-information law of large numbers.
